newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU presidency cautious on sulphur-in-fuel plan.
newsitem.headline: EU presidency cautious on sulphur-in-fuel plan.

text.p: A plan by Sweden and Finland to push for stricter norms on sulphur content in vehicle fuels is unlikely to win widespread EU support, Dutch Housing and Environment Minister Margreet de Boer said on Tuesday.

"As a Dutch environment minister I must admit that I can probably fully endorse the Swedish view. The Netherlands is pretty much on the same wavelength but as chairman of the environment council I have to say that that view will probably not be shared by all the member states," de Boer said.
The Dutch minister was speaking at a briefing ahead of the March 2-4 meeting of EU environment ministers.
"Probably we will have to find a middle way though if we could take significant steps towards the Swedish view then the Netherlands would be quite happy with that," de Boer said.

She was referring to a demand by Sweden and Finland for stricter norms on sulphur content in diesel and petrol after a study they sponsored said introduction costs would not be as high as previously thought.
Swedish Environment Minister Anna Lindh and her Finnish counterpart Pekka Haavisto based their arguments on the outcome of a study by consultants Arthur D Little.

Study findings put the capital investment cost of cutting sulphur content in road transport gasoline to 30 parts per million (ppm) at 2.94 billion European currency units, 17 percent less than the European Commission's own research data.
Cutting sulphur content in diesel to 50 ppm would cost 5.99 billion or 55 percent less than the Commission figure, it said.

Lindh and Haavisto said the existing Commission proposals on sulphur content, setting average market-value targets for the year 2000 at 150 ppm for petrol and 300 ppm for diesel, would inhibit the introduction of direct-injection engines and their potential for fuel savings.
The original draft rules, contained in the EU's so-called auto-oil programme, set out a series of quality standards for fuel and engine emission standards required by the year 2000.
